subject: After-action: service recovery summary & mitigations roadmap
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Meyers <alicia.meyers@clearstream.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: After-action: service recovery summary & mitigations roadmap

Alicia —

Thank you again for your patience this morning. I wanted to share our post-incident summary and the immediate mitigation roadmap so Clearstream has a single source of truth while we complete the deeper technical RCA. Below is a concise synopsis, timeline highlights, and clear next steps with owners and ETA. I’ve attached the preliminary log bundle and timeline CSV for your engineers.

Summary (what happened)
- Incident window: 2026-11-03T08:02:00Z — 2026-11-03T09:48:00Z (~1h46m).
- Impact: elevated request latencies and token duplication/response retries affecting approximately 65 customer accounts (peak error rate ~12% on the serving tier). Clearstream experienced increased generation latencies and a small number of duplicated generation events; no customer data was exposed.

Root cause (short version)
- A race between our autoscaler orchestration and a state-sync job led to stale KV cache snapshots on a subset of dedicated inference nodes. When the autoscaler performed a rapid pool shuffle during a high-load period, certain requests were routed to instances with an inconsistent KV cache. The inconsistency triggered token replays and internal retries, amplifying load and pushing latency beyond SLOs.

Immediate remediation completed
- Rolled back the affected autoscaler policy and reverted to the previous stable pool configuration (completed 08:25 UTC).
- Deployed a hotfix that blocks request routing to nodes with unverified KV snapshots (deployed 08:42 UTC).
- Increased request throttling for non-critical background workloads to reduce pressure on control-plane syncs (08:50 UTC).

Timeline (high level)
- 08:02 UTC: First alerts — elevated latencies on serving tier.
- 08:12 UTC: Escalation to on-call; pattern analysis begins.
- 08:25 UTC: Autoscaler policy rollback.
- 08:42 UTC: Hotfix deployed to route around nodes with stale KV caches.
- 09:10 UTC: Error rates fall below threshold; monitoring confirms steady-state.
- 09:48 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; post-incident monitoring period initiated.

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Short-term (this week):
  • Rishi (rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai) — Complete deterministic test that reproduces autoscaler+state-sync race and publish runbook (ETA: 2026-11-06).
  • Platform — Harden routing to verify KV snapshot freshness before accepting new requests (in progress; ETA: 2026-11-05).
- Mid-term (30 days):
  • Marissa (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) — Configuration audit of dedicated pool autoscaler policies and new safety gates (ETA: 2026-12-03).
  • Reliability Eng — Add end-to-end e2e for rapid reshuffle scenarios and include in nightly stress-campaigns (ETA: 2026-12-05).
- Customer-facing (this month):
  • Kimberly (me) — Follow up with a full technical RCA (public and account-level versions) and proposed SLA credit approach (ETA: 2026-11-10).

What we’re sharing today
- Attached: support_log_bundle_20261103.zip (sanitized logs), timeline_UTC.csv.
- Draft public-facing RCA: https://redwood.app/drive/incident-20261103-postmortem (linked for convenience; we will publish the public version after your review).

Alicia — I know Clearstream relies on predictable latency. We will commit to the action items above and propose a follow-up sync for next Tuesday to walk through the full technical RCA and the proposed customer credit. Please let me know if you’d prefer an earlier call.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: support_log_bundle_20261103.zip, timeline_UTC.csv
From: Alicia Meyers <alicia.meyers@clearstream.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: After-action: service recovery summary & mitigations roadmap

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the quick summary and the attachments. A couple quick questions: 1) Can you confirm whether any tokens or customer payloads were written to external logs or shared storage during the event? 2) What is your proposed credit estimate for Clearstream under the SLA? 3) Can we get a short (15–20 min) sync today with an engineer who can walk through the hotfix and confirm the mitigation guarantees?

We’ll review the attached timeline with our ops team and flag anything that needs deeper analysis on our end.

—Alicia Meyers
Director, Platform Reliability
Clearstream
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Meyers <alicia.meyers@clearstream.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: After-action: service recovery summary & mitigations roadmap

Alicia — quick answers below; I’ll follow up in detail during the RCA call.

1) Data exposure: Confirmed no customer payloads were exfiltrated. The issue was an internal state-sync inconsistency; the logs we attached have been sanitized and do not include raw customer inputs. Our legal/compliance team will provide a formal statement if you need it for audit purposes.

2) SLA credit: We propose a provisional credit of 6.5% of November invoice prorated for the impacted window for customers in affected capacity tiers. This is an initial estimate; I’ll put a final recommendation in writing in the account-level RCA doc (ETA 2026-11-10).

3) Short sync: Yes — Rishi can join a 20-minute call today at 15:00 PT to walk through the hotfix behavior and routing guarantees. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Additional context: we have quarantined and preserved the affected node images and control-plane traces; we will share those artifacts with your SREs under an NDA if desired. The hotfix we pushed is non-destructive: requests are routed to only-verified nodes; it prevents new KV snapshot adoption until a verification handshake completes.

Next deliverables we’ll send you
- Full technical RCA (account + public) with root-cause evidence (ETA: 2026-11-10).
- Post-incident verification checklist and scheduled compliance attestation (ETA: 2026-11-12).

I’ll send the meeting invite for 15:00 PT unless you prefer a different time.

Best,
Kimberly

Attachments: hotfix_patch.diff
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Clearstream follow-ups & owner confirmations (do not forward)

Team —

Recap from the external thread (for context): Clearstream saw elevated latencies and token duplication due to the autoscaler+state-sync race. They want a 15–20 min deep-dive today and a formal SLA credit recommendation in the account RCA.

Immediate asks from me (please confirm ownership/reply-all):
- Rishi: Lead the technical walk-through at 15:00 PT and prepare two slides: hotfix behavior and verification tests. Confirmed?
- Marissa: Draft the configuration audit notes and proposed autoscaler safety-gates. I need a one-page summary by COB Friday (ETA: 2026-11-06).
- Engineering Legal/Compliance: Coordinate the sanitized artifact package and confirm NDA language. I’ll loop in legal after you confirm they need it.

Also: please update HUBSPOT-4321 with the mitigation artifacts and put the provisional SLA credit amount in the billing notes (this will be finalized in the RCA doc).

Thanks — Kim

Note: This internal mail contains sensitive details; do not forward to external participants without approval.
